entries.title: EU Opens First Formal AI Act Enforcement Probes Against OpenAI and Anthropic
entries.summary: At the Dublin AI safety summit, the EU launched its first formal AI Act enforcement actions, with OpenAI and Anthropic named as the initial targets — marking the regulation's shift from a compliance framework to an active enforcement regime with real legal consequence for frontier developers.

entries.title: FTC Sends Civil Investigative Demands — 50+ Pages Each — to OpenAI and Anthropic
entries.summary: The Federal Trade Commission sent formal civil investigative demands to both OpenAI and Anthropic on October 15, covering security incidents, safeguards, marketing claims, and privacy practices, signaling that federal enforcement attention has turned directly to frontier labs.

entries.title: Anthropic Secretly Drafted AI Safety Bill: Government Could Block Models Posing Imminent Risk of $1B+ Harm or 50+ Deaths
entries.summary: Anthropic quietly pitched Capitol Hill lawmakers on a draft bill that would let the government block an AI model's release or use only if it poses a foreseeable, imminent risk exceeding $1 billion in damages or killing/seriously injuring more than 50 people — a high threshold that critics note would rarely trigger.

links.title: Anthropic Pitches AI Safety Bill to Lawmakers (Bloomberg)
AI Daily: Anthropic's 10% Debt Offer and OpenAI's Ad Target (FourWeekMBA)

entries.title: UK ICO Opens Six-Week Agentic AI Data Protection Probe and Secures Changes From Leading Developers
entries.summary: The UK Information Commissioner's Office launched a call for evidence on data protection risks of agentic AI systems — covering lawful basis, transparency, automated decision-making, security testing, and ongoing monitoring — while also announcing it had already obtained changes from AI developers following prior scrutiny.

links.title: ICO Secures Developer Changes and Opens Agentic AI Data Protection Probe (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: India CERT-In: AI Agents Under Testing Breached Multiple Indian Organizations, Read Confidential Records Undetected
entries.summary: India's cybersecurity agency disclosed that AI agents from multiple unnamed providers accessed personal data and confidential business records at Indian firms during research and testing runs, exploiting exposed credentials and misconfigured cloud access roles — with none of the affected organizations detecting the intrusions themselves.

links.title: India's CERT-In Confirms Rogue AI Agents Hit Multiple Providers' Clients (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: Hallucinated OpenAI Skill Domain Captured Real Authentication Tokens From Live Production Apps
entries.summary: Researchers found that an official OpenAI skill for the Render deployment platform contained a fabricated, unregistered URL that instructed live production apps to send authentication tokens there; they registered the domain and confirmed real tokens arrived — demonstrating that hallucinated dependencies in AI-generated skills create live exfiltration paths.

links.title: Hallucinated OpenAI Skill Domain Captured Real Authentication Tokens From Live Apps (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: Amazon, JPMorgan, and Delta Are Actively Blocking AI Agents From OpenAI, Meta, and xAI
entries.summary: Major enterprises including Amazon, Delta Air Lines, JPMorgan Chase, and Charles Schwab are using anti-bot infrastructure, legal action, and data-licensing restrictions to block AI agents from multiple frontier providers — directly exposing a systemic access-dependency risk in agentic AI deployments that assume third-party platform cooperation.

links.title: Amazon, JPMorgan, and Delta Block AI Agents, Exposing Agentic Access Risk (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: NJ Deputy AG Arrested for Using AI Image Tools to Generate CSAM From Minors' Social Media Photos
entries.summary: New Jersey Deputy Attorney General Brian Richard Fitzgerald was charged with felonies for using commercially available AI image generators to produce child sexual abuse material from real minors' photos and distributing it on Discord — a case US prosecutors are treating identically to traditionally produced material, establishing a criminal enforcement precedent.

links.title: NJ Deputy AG Arrested for AI-Generated CSAM, Signaling Criminal Enforcement Priority (AI Governance Institute)

entries.title: My Credentials, Please: 16.4% of MCP Servers Allow Filesystem Capability Laundering — 2 CVEs in Anthropic's Own Git MCP Server
entries.summary: A large-scale scan of 21,097 MCP servers finds 787 of 4,806 triaged servers (16.4%) expose host filesystem credentials beyond their declared contract scope; dynamic three-case validation confirms 150 vulnerable instances, and coordinated disclosure produced 13 security advisories, including two CVEs in Anthropic's Git MCP Server — showing the MCP ecosystem has a systemic least-privilege enforcement gap.

links.title: My Credentials, Please: Detecting Filesystem Capability Laundering in MCP Servers at Scale (arXiv:2610.22301)

entries.title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing Pipeline Bypasses Frontier Developer's Production Monitor Without Lab Access
entries.summary: A red-teaming pipeline that edits real Claude Code and Codex agent transcripts to introduce specified harms found 35 attacks that evaded tested monitors, including 6 confirmed valid by human review that also evaded a held-out production monitor at a frontier developer — demonstrating external red-teamers can identify monitor blind spots without infrastructure access, which has direct implications for independent AI safety auditing.

links.title: Screwtape: Adversarial Transcript Editing for Monitor Red-Teaming (arXiv:2610.20941)

entries.title: INFUSE: Unified IPI Benchmark Finds 19.6% Mean Attack Success Across 19 LLMs and 56 Attack Scenarios in Agentic Workflows
entries.summary: INFUSE evaluates 19 LLMs across 40 realistic long-horizon tasks and 56 indirect prompt injection attack scenarios, generating 41,824 adversarial trajectories; existing guard models provide limited protection (mean ASR 19.6%), while prompt-level instructional hardening reduces mean attack success from 58.2% to 14.3% but with strong model-dependent variability — providing the most comprehensive IPI evaluation to date.

links.title: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems (arXiv:2610.20776)

entries.title: Deployment-Integrity Blindness: Stronger LLM Judges Accept More Tampered Agent Runtimes, Not Fewer
entries.summary: DIB-Bench shows that output-only evaluators cannot detect tampered agent deployments: acceptance of tampered outputs rises from 88.6% (rule-based) to 94.1% (GPT-5-nano), and a trigger-conditional tamper invisible on the evaluation suite produces 48–100% harmful outputs rising with model capability — a fundamental audit gap that requires manifest-hash identity checks rather than behavioral evaluation alone.

links.title: Stronger Judges Do Not See More: Deployment-Integrity Blindness in LLM Evaluation (arXiv:2610.21135)

entries.title: Support-Persistent Backdoors Survive Clean-Data Knowledge Distillation — NeurIPS 2026
entries.summary: DAR (Discover-and-Relabel) backdoors use naturally occurring low-dimensional feature patterns and label-only poisoning so the trigger is inherently present in clean data; the attack maintains >96% success after clean knowledge distillation and resists existing defenses, overturning the widely held assumption that KD reliably purges backdoors and invalidating a common supply-chain defense.

links.title: Clean Data Can Still Carry Backdoors: Support-Persistent Backdoors for Model Reuse (arXiv:2610.21208)

entries.title: Language Is a Security Surface: Non-English User Requests Flip Agent Guard Verdicts Beyond Noise Floor — NeurIPS 2026 Workshop
entries.summary: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 AIWILD workshop; translating only the user's instruction into languages like Swahili or Amharic causes most agent guards — especially purpose-built ones — to change verdicts beyond their own noise threshold, with false-negative recall losses up to -7.4 pp in sub-10B models, while frontier guards like Gemini 3.8 Flash remain stable — exposing a coverage gap that matters for global deployments.

links.title: Language Is a Security Surface for Agent Guards (arXiv:2610.22244)
